key_insight: A general-relativistic superfluid framework establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity, enabling stable simulations of neutron-star vortex dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides a foundation for computational studies of superfluid rotation and angular-momentum transfer relevant to pulsar glitches and neutron-star binaries.
method: Include entrainment, vortex forces, and line energy in relativistic two-fluid hydrodynamics.
Recast vortex dynamics using effective electromagnetic fields and drift velocities.
Combine finite-volume evolution with constrained transport of vorticity and implicit electric-field updates.
evidence_signal: Validation includes an exact relativistic superfluid Riemann solution, Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, and oscillation modes of global two-fluid neutron-star equilibria.
watch_item: The spin-down demonstration prescribes vortex release and repinning; commonly used dissipative force-balanced models without line tension are also shown to be generically ill-posed at short wavelengths.
paper_title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
